item.title: Search underway after Indonesian passenger ship loses contact
item.description: Indonesian rescuers launched a search operation after authorities lost contact with a passenger ship carrying more than 240 people in the Java Sea.

item.title: Deputies respond to trespasser at Malibu home of Kamala Harris
item.description: A trespasser was reported at former Vice President Kamala Harris' Malibu, California, home.

item.title: Iran-backed Houthis tighten grip on key oil shipping lane
item.description: The moves by the Houthis make it easier for the Iran-backed rebels to target ships transiting the crucial Bab el-Mandeb Strait for Saudi Arabian oil exports.

item.title: Elena Rybakina bests defending champion Aryna Sabalenka to win her first U.S. Open
item.description: Aryna Sabalenka, the two-time defending U.S. Open champion, was dethroned Saturday, losing to Elena Rybakina in three sets.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Sept. 13)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Anthropic CEO says "exponential" growth of AI is a "warning sign"
item.description: Artificial intelligence technology is developing at an "exponential" rate, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told CBS News, calling the situation a "warning sign" for the industry that requires serious safeguards.

item.title: Anthropic CEO calls for competitors to agree to "third-party evaluators" in push for AI safety
item.description: In an interview with CBS News, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei encouraged the artificial intelligence industry to come together in the pursuit of safeguards. Watch the interview on "CBS Sunday Morning" on Sept. 13.

item.title: Anthropic CEO says he didn't appreciate how fast AI would progress
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told CBS News that he didn't fully anticipate the effects of rapid artificial intelligence development, while also encouraging the public not to panic. Watch the interview on "CBS Sunday Morning" on Sept. 13.

item.title: Celine Dion overcomes rare neurological disorder to perform first concert in 6 years
item.description: Celine Dion's return to the stage underscored a remarkable comeback after stiff-person syndrome, an incurable condition that causes stiffness and cramps, forced her to cancel shows and cast years of uncertainty over whether she would ever perform again.

item.title: Photographer remembers capturing one of 9/11's defining images
item.description: A photographer who documented the horror of 9/11 reflects on how he captured a defining image of the tragedy and the significance of the photo 25 years later. Bradley Blackburn reports.

item.title: Why flowers are placed on some names at the 9/11 Memorial
item.description: As the nation marks 25 years since the 9/11 terror attacks, Jarred Hill takes a look at how the memorial in New York honors the lives of those who died year round through the birthday flowers program.

item.title: Millennials might be bringing back the minivan
item.description: SUVs have long dominated the family car market -- but an old-school favorite is pulling back into the picture. Minivans are seeing a huge sales surge as a new generation is giving the family hauler another look. Evyn Moon explains what's driving the comeback.

item.title: Putin warns Europe against sending troops to Ukraine
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin warned that sending European troops into Ukraine would amount to direct conflict with Russia.

item.title: U.S. women beat Spain 76-66 to reach the FIBA World Cup final against France
item.description: Breanna Stewart scored 16 points and Kahleah Copper added 13 to help the U.S. beat Spain 76-66, advancing to the championship game of the women's FIBA World Cup.

item.title: Trump says he would "love" a unified Ireland as he kicks off visit
item.description: President Trump's visit to Ireland mixes official talks with Irish leaders and attendance at the Irish Open at a golf course that the president owns.

item.title: Former Army secretary praises Ukraine in 1st public appearance since resigning
item.description: During his 18 months as Army secretary, Dan Driscoll pushed the U.S. military to apply lessons from the war in Ukraine.

item.title: President Trump's childhood home sells after renovation
item.description: The president lived at the Tudor-style Queens estate until age 4.

item.title: How to find a good financial planner
item.description: Jill Schlesinger answers your personal finance questions.

item.title: Artist captures destruction, pain and recovery in historic Ground Zero sketches
item.description: Artist John Coburn went to Ground Zero after the 9/11 attacks, drawing the scenes of destruction, recovery, and everyday life there as a way to transmute pain into art. Coburn spoke with Nicole Sganga about his "Healing Hearts" collection, which he sent to families of victims, survivors and first responders.

item.title: NFL season preview with Joe Musso
item.description: CBS Sports' Joe Musso looks ahead as the NFL season ramps up.

item.description: Tune in Sunday at 7:30p ET/PT for a 60 Minutes hidden camera investigation into a lucrative business: brokering pardons for felons. Lobbyists offer a chance at clemency — at a cost, and with no guarantees.

item.description: Known for his bold, innovative cooking, Chef Dale Talde built his career on Asian flavors. His Filipino roots, Midwest upbringing and love of Chinese cuisine all come together at Goosefeather.

item.description: An El Niño pattern occurs every two to seven years.

item.title: Chicago rapper Lil Durk acquitted in Los Angeles murder-for-hire plot
item.description: A federal jury in Los Angeles has acquitted Grammy-winning Chicago rapper Lil Durk in a murder-for-hire plot targeting another rapper.

item.title: CIA declassifies dozens of never-before-seen 9/11 documents
item.description: The CIA released 71 reports from the months and years leading up to 9/11, providing a new look at what the spy agency told two presidents before the deadly strikes.

item.title: Afghan woman dubbed an "alien terrorist" deported in obscure court's first case
item.description: An Afghan permanent resident living in Texas has been deported after the Justice Department accused her of being an "alien terrorist," in the first such case of its kind.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy juror reveals more about lone holdout
item.description: A mistrial was declared in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy after jurors could not reach a unanimous decision. One of the jurors shares details on their deliberations in an interview with Gayle King.
